resolutions.resolution: ::first-line / ::first-letter don't apply to input / textarea for now, revisit once we have better-defined layout for them
irc: <fantasai> emilio: Blink only supports :first-line somehow
<fantasai> emilio: It feels weird. I almost changed this in Gecko accidentally, while fixing support for field-sizing.
<fantasai> emilio: Spec is ambiguous, but I wouldn't expect it to dig into contents of a replaced element.
<lea> q?
<fantasai> emilio: So I think we should be explicit that they don't apply to replaced elements, same way as ::before/::after don't apply
<tantek> presumably our reasoning on this is specific to inputs rather than generalizing to say, any use of contenteditable?
<fantasai> astearns: I don't see a problem with ::first-letter, but ::first-line seems odd
<lea> q+
<fantasai> emilio: I would prefer not to support any of them. I'm half-sure it is accidental in Blink.
<astearns> ack lea
<PaulG> order matters, if you put scrollLeft first, it will scroll left but not up. So, I understand now.
<emilio> lea: from an author-facing perspective they expect it to work
<fantasai> lea: From author-facing, I think if they're using it they're expecting it to work
<emilio> ... not sure that's undesirable
<emilio> ... the argument they're replaced elements make sense
<emilio> ... I wish ::before / ::after would work
<emilio> ... if we could make it work that'd be the better outcome
<tantek> do those pseudos work on a contenteditable element?
<emilio> ... do we want to put theoretical purity
<emilio> ... I don't see a huge user need
<emilio> ... so if it complicates implementations I don't think it's worth it
<PaulG> q+
<emilio> ... no strong opinion either way
<PaulG> q-
<fantasai> emilio: They do work on contenteditable
<fantasai> emilio: Big issue is that the layout is not fun.
<lea> s/do we want to put theoretical purity/per the PoC, do we want to put theoretical purity above author needs?/
<dbaron> the proposal seems reasonable to me; I don't think ::first-letter and ::first-line make much sense in input and textarea
<fantasai> emilio: Even without auto appearance, the way these elements are laid out internally is not specced and does not match across implementations
<fantasai> emilio: Making them work reliably is sketchy
<fantasai> emilio: There are some extra elements, for example, in a password input. Is that part of the ::first-line or not?
<fantasai> emilio: I think the real issue is, same for ::before/::after, they shouldn't work because we don't have interoperable layout for these elements
<TabAtkins> +1 to emilio here
<fantasai> emilio: Need to define how it interacts with ::placeholder, etc. etc.
<fantasai> emilio: Internal contents of these elements are not defined per spec
<fantasai> +1 to emilio
<kbabbitt> +1 to emilio
<emilio> astearns: I think we should define these not to work for now given that
<schenney> I suspect the Chrome behavior is an accidental artifact of recent changes to the internal layout structure of text areas. If so definitely something not easy to spec. +1 to emilio.
<tantek> not apply for now is reasonable because we can expand it in the future with new information
<emilio> RESOLVED: ::first-line / ::first-letter don't apply to input / textarea for now, revisit once we have better-defined layout for them

fresh.title: [css-gaps-1] Define rule-break: normal for grid lanes containers
fresh.background: The `normal` initial value is defined per container type: for **grid**, a decoration starts and ends at "T" intersections (it stops when it meets an item spanning across the gap) but continues through "cross" intersections; for **flex**, `normal` behaves like `none` (each line's decorations are continuous and independent). Grid lanes containers are not yet covered.
